newsitem.title: CANADA: Australian securities chief sees global agency.
newsitem.headline: Australian securities chief sees global agency.

text.p: Globalization and electronic trading will soon force governments to consider setting up a world regulatory body, Australian Securities Commission chairman Alan Cameron said on Wednesday.

"We already have examples of trans-national regulation of financial markets, such as the common futures market operating in Australia and New Zealand," he told the annual meeting of the International Organization of Securities Commissions.
Regulators now operate within national boundaries and have loosely knit international agreements, he said.
"But now national and regional bodies cannot meet the challenges of global electronic trading and sooner rather than later we must face up to the need for a super-national regulatory body," he said.

"Much progress is being made toward harmonization of accounting and reporting standards and I know there is strong resistance to a super national body. But it's the only way we can move forward to orderly world capital markets and protection of the investing public," he said.
